rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This body edit re-verified: chunk 34, line 480, now reads "The M5 lecture *Hooks always fire* names that property." "M5" as module shorthand is not a fresh referent here — it first appears at chunk 10, line 209 ("M2 exercise...M1 deliberately runs"), and recurs at chunks 12, 15, 17, 29 before chunk 34 reaches it; a sequential reader already holds the M-number convention. The lecture is additionally named by its own title (italicized "Hooks always fire"), which is the strongest form rule 1 asks for, not merely positional. Chunk 37, line 566, names both source files directly in backticks (`hooks-always-fire.md`, `what-packaging-is.md`) inside the same sentence that describes them — no unresolved referent. Second closest call, unchanged by this diff: chunk 20 "/goal", line 328, "The runtime-shipped sibling of the verifier you author later in the training" — "the verifier" is not named earlier in this file, but reads as arc-earned spine vocabulary (M6 pairing established in chunk 42's "Related AE101 modules" map, and the same forward-trust pattern the file already uses for "un-packaged send-off"/"packaging"). No unresolved referent found across all 43 chunks on this pass.

Chunk 34 line 480 is stronger post-diff than the version this class last judged: the old text ("The closing lecture on packaging names that property") described the source by role/position; the new text names it by module ("The M5 lecture") AND exact title (*Hooks always fire*) in the same sentence — passes cleanly, no position-dependence left. Chunk 37 line 566 goes further still and names both source files by their literal filenames in backticks, immediately adjacent to what each one does ("M5's pre-exercise lecture (`hooks-always-fire.md`) names hooks as the runtime primitive; the closer (`what-packaging-is.md`) carries Cherny's shell-hook verifier shape"). Verified both files exist and are wired into the M5 module (`grep -n 'hooks-always-fire\|what-packaging-is' curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/learn-from-the-test.md` → both present as `[Lecture: ...]` includes). No bare "the opening lecture said..."-style positional pointer anywhere in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This file is a lookup surface ("Flat look-up for the primitives AE101 leans on", line 3), so §9's per-slide bold-count budget is waived by the rule's own reference/supplementary-page exception; the handle-cap sub-clause still binds. The two edited lines (480, 566) carry no new bold spans — the diff changed only plain prose between the pre-existing bolds (`**must**`, `**recommended**`, `**AE101 cross-refs:**`), all of which predate this pass and were already covered by the prior instance's PASS. Same open tension noted then, unaffected by this diff: several bolded leads elsewhere in the file (e.g. chunk 18 line 318, 13 words) run past a strict \u2272 5-word handle, but the compliant label-only shape exists in the same file (chunk 31's `**`/clear`**`) proving it's reachable, and the harm test in the dispatch preamble reads these as the scannable payload a lookup entry needs rather than decorative — not filed as REVISE, this remains a standing rule question for the maintainer on the general lookup-bold shape, not something this diff introduced or worsened.
